purpose: Current structural benchmark for Free Reliable Appliance Pickup. Copy the architecture lessons, not competitor wording or unsupported service claims.

observedPages.lesson: State pages route users downward instead of trying to own every city query.
The state hub is a routing layer; city pages own local intent.
Regional hubs support city pages rather than duplicating each city page.
City page owns one location with a concise transaction path and local context.
Commercial and appliance-specific intents are linked from the city owner but do not replace it.
Unique local facts and official alternatives distinguish Fresno from neighboring city pages.
Exact city ownership is reinforced with locally specific information and appliance paths.
Commercial intent has its own hierarchy rather than being repeated heavily on every residential city page.

freeReliableRules: Use original wording and real business qualification rules.
Do not copy competitor claims that all appliances or broken units qualify.
General city owner pages should own broad city appliance-pickup/removal intent.
Specialty washer/dryer, refrigerator, freezer and stove pages should remain narrow.
State, county and regional hubs should route authority to exact city owners.
Preserve real photos, correct phone routing, Formspree request flow and people-first local details.
Judge success with finalized GSC and regular organic query-to-page ownership.
